system_description.narrative_title: Tariffs and trade realignment: US–Canada–EU frictions
system_description.narrative_summary: An emerging crisis of tariff-driven trade friction and strategic economic realignment among the United States, Canada and the European Union dominates the window. As political incentives in the US push tariff measures and carve-outs, affected firms and partner states seek alternative partners and supply‑chain diversification, generating feedbacks across negotiations, industrial policy, and diplomatic summits. The system is open: policy levers, corporate responses, international negotiations, media and electoral politics continuously exchange information and influence each other, producing reinforcing and balancing loops (tariffs → industry harm → political pressure → negotiated relief or escalation).
system_description.scope: Trade policy decisions, tariffs and carve-outs; bilateral/multilateral trade negotiations (US‑Canada, Canada‑EU, EU‑US); corporate reactions in manufacturing and aerospace; supply‑chain dependencies (aluminum, autos, rare earths); summit diplomacy and public political messaging within the North Atlantic economic space.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economic order (international trade system and great‑power economic competition)
adjacent_subsystems: US domestic politics and electoral incentives
EU internal cohesion and industrial policy (aerospace, critical minerals)
Global supply chains and critical minerals/manufacturing sectors
Canada's trade diversification and domestic industry politics

variables.name: Tariff intensity
variables.description: The average level of tariff rates and tariff coverage applied across affected trade relationships.

variables.name: Market access restrictions
variables.description: The prevalence and severity of non‑tariff barriers and regulatory measures that limit cross-border market access.

variables.name: Negotiation intensity
variables.description: The frequency, scope and resource intensity of ongoing bilateral and multilateral trade negotiations.

variables.name: Supply‑chain concentration
variables.description: The degree to which production and inputs depend on a small number of external suppliers or locations for critical components.

variables.name: Supplier diversification rate
variables.description: The pace at which firms change or add alternative suppliers and sourcing geographies to reduce concentration.

variables.name: Corporate relocation rate
variables.description: The rate at which firms relocate production, shift plant footprints, or reconfigure supply lines across borders.

variables.name: Industrial capacity utilization
variables.description: The utilization and available productive capacity within industries sensitive to trade measures (e.g., manufacturing, aerospace).

variables.name: Industrial subsidy and aid level
variables.description: The overall magnitude of public financial support, loans and targeted industrial assistance directed toward affected sectors.

variables.name: Political pressure for relief
variables.description: The intensity of public, legislative and stakeholder demands on policymakers to reduce trade measures or provide carve‑outs.

variables.name: Protectionist political incentive
variables.description: The strength of political incentives and motivations to adopt protectionist measures for domestic economic or electoral advantage.

variables.name: Media and public salience
variables.description: The volume and prominence of media coverage and public discourse about trade tensions and related economic impacts.

variables.name: Diplomatic and summit activity
variables.description: The occurrence and prominence of high‑level diplomatic meetings and summits aimed at managing trade relations.

variables.name: Trade realignment velocity
variables.description: The speed at which trade flows, sourcing relationships and partner networks are reoriented in response to policy changes.

variables.name: Critical materials access
variables.description: The security and diversity of supply for strategic inputs and critical minerals necessary for key industries.

variables.name: Trade dispute risk perception
variables.description: The perceived likelihood and expected severity of formal trade disputes, retaliatory measures or escalation between partners.

variables.name: Supply‑chain disruption risk
variables.description: The perceived and modeled risk that policy measures or shocks will cause interruptions to the movement of goods and inputs.

catalysts.title: Canada–EU Carney summit
catalysts.description: High‑level Canada–EU summit expected to address trade ties and the 'associate member' spat; could shape declarations and short‑term cooperation or friction.
catalysts.rationale: Spat over 'associate member' label and headlines saying spat will overshadow Carney summit (2026-10-28, 2026-10-29).

catalysts.title: U.S. removal of some Canada tariffs
catalysts.description: Administration action to lift selected tariffs on Canada as reported; will immediately lower tariff exposure for affected sectors.
catalysts.rationale: Headline reports 'Trump to Remove Some Tariffs on Canada' and related coverage (2026-10-29).

catalysts.title: Ongoing US–Canada trade negotiations
catalysts.description: Continuing bilateral talks with limited progress reported; will drive negotiation intensity and influence medium‑term policy outcomes.
catalysts.rationale: Canada reports limited progress in trade talks with US (2026-10-28).

catalysts.title: EU Airbus loan dispute escalation
catalysts.description: EU financial support to Airbus risks breaking a trade truce with the U.S., potentially prompting retaliatory measures or negotiations.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EU loan to Airbus threatens trade truce with US' and reports of Airbus work with EU states (2026-10-28, 2026-10-29).

catalysts.title: Tariff relief tied to U.S. Audi factory deal
catalysts.description: Administration promises tariff concessions to secure an Audi plant; implementation or formalization could shift tariffs and investment incentives.
catalysts.rationale: Exclusive report: Administration promised tariff relief in talks to secure U.S. Audi factory (2026-10-30).

catalysts.title: EU push to diversify rare earths and critical materials
catalysts.description: EU and member states accelerate efforts to reduce dependence on China for rare earths; a multi‑year program altering sourcing and investment.
catalysts.rationale: France envoy: rare earths diversification possible in 3–5 years; EU weighs mirroring US on securing critical minerals (2026-10-28).

catalysts.title: U.S. robotics national‑security scrutiny
catalysts.description: Administration signals national‑security risk findings on imported robotics; may trigger regulations or market restrictions without immediate tariffs.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Trump says imported robotics pose national security risks but does not impose tariffs' (2026-10-29).

catalysts.title: Canada pursues new trade partners
catalysts.description: Canada's active deals (e.g., UAE) and diplomacy aim to reorient trade relationships, reducing reliance on strained partners.
catalysts.rationale: Canada signs trade deal with UAE as Carney seeks new trading partners (2026-10-28).

catalysts.title: Threat of very high auto tariffs on Canada
catalysts.description: Public warnings and political rhetoric keep possibility of steep auto tariffs alive; decision to impose or retract would strongly move industry outcomes.
catalysts.rationale: Honda warns 50% Canada auto tariffs would be catastrophic; political headlines keep threat alive (2026-10-28).
